newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Main provisions of EU work time directive.
newsitem.headline: Main provisions of EU work time directive.

text.p: The European Union's working time directive, which was upheld by the European Court of Justice on Tuesday, sets the following rules to protect workers' health and safety:
-- An average maximum work week of 48 hours, including overtime. The average can be based on a period of up to four months. Workers may put in more than 48 hours on a voluntary basis.
-- A minimum daily rest period of 11 consecutive hours.
-- A minimum uninterrupted rest period of 24 hours per week. The court struck down a provision requiring the rest period to include Sunday in principle.
-- Paid annual leave of at least four weeks.
-- An average shift of eight hours for night workers.

Workers in a wide range of transport sectors, sea workers and doctors in training are not covered by the rules. Governments can also exempt managing executives. Employees in the home and religious officials are also exempted from some provisions.
